question: In addition to a PFD, what equipment does New York law require on a personal watercraft to help prevent an engine backfire from igniting fuel vapors?
choice_a: A supplemental fire extinguisher rated for gasoline fires only
choice_b: A secondary bilge pump wired to a separate battery
choice_c: A catalytic converter identical to those used in automobiles
choice_d: A Coast Guard-approved backfire flame arrestor
explanation: New York Navigation Law Section 73-a requires PWCs to carry a Coast Guard-approved backfire flame arrestor to help prevent an engine backfire from igniting flammable vapors in the engine compartment.
source_note: NY Navigation Law Section 73-a(1)(b), backfire arrestor requirement

question: What ventilation does New York law require in a PWC's engine and fuel compartments, unless those spaces are naturally exposed to open air?
choice_a: At least two ventilator ducts or cowls designed to remove flammable gases and vapors from the compartments
choice_b: A single vent hole no larger than one inch in diameter
choice_c: No ventilation is required on any PWC under 10 feet long
choice_d: A continuously running electric exhaust fan, with no cowl or duct required
explanation: Section 73-a requires at least two ventilator cowls (or an equivalent system) to clear flammable gases from a PWC's enclosed engine and fuel compartments, unless the bilge is naturally exposed to open air.
source_note: NY Navigation Law Section 73-a(1)(c)(i), ventilation requirement

question: What kind of sound-producing device does New York law require a PWC to carry?
choice_a: A referee-style whistle only, with no minimum audible distance specified
choice_b: A mechanical, non-siren device capable of producing a blast of two seconds or more, audible for at least half a mile in calm conditions
choice_c: No sound-producing device is required on a PWC because it has no cabin to store one
choice_d: A siren identical to those used on emergency vehicles
explanation: New York Navigation Law Section 73-a requires PWCs to carry a mechanical sound-producing appliance, other than a siren, able to produce a blast of at least two seconds that is audible for at least half a mile under normal conditions.
source_note: NY Navigation Law Section 73-a(1)(c)(ii), sound device requirement

question: Besides a sound device, what visual distress signal must be aboard a personal watercraft in New York?
choice_a: A green flare gun loaded with at least three flares
choice_b: A white strobe light mounted on the bow that is only required after dark
choice_c: A fluorescent-orange distress flag at least one foot square, or an equivalent Coast Guard-approved visual distress signal
choice_d: No visual distress signal is required aboard any PWC
explanation: New York Navigation Law Section 73-a requires a fluorescent-orange distress flag measuring at least one foot square, or an equivalent Coast Guard-approved visual distress signal, to be carried aboard a PWC.
source_note: NY Navigation Law Section 73-a(1)(c)(iii), visual distress signal requirement

question: How close may a PWC operate to a New York designated bathing/swimming area?
choice_a: As close as 50 feet, at any speed
choice_b: There is no minimum distance as long as the operator sounds the horn first
choice_c: PWCs must stay at least one full nautical mile from any bathing area at all times, with no exceptions
choice_d: Not within 500 feet, except when launching from a designated site or crossing narrow waters where the opposite shore is closer than 500 feet, in which case speed is capped at 10 mph
explanation: New York Navigation Law Section 73-a bars PWC operation within 500 feet of a designated swimming area, with a narrow-waterway exception that caps speed at 10 mph and permits launching from designated sites.
source_note: NY Navigation Law Section 73-a(1)(f), bathing area distance restriction

question: What is the minimum age at which a livery in New York may legally rent a PWC to a customer, separate from the minimum age to operate one?
choice_b: 14 years old, the same as the minimum operating age
choice_c: 12 years old, if a parent is present at the livery
choice_d: There is no minimum rental age, only a minimum operating age
explanation: While the minimum age to operate a PWC in New York is 14, Section 73-a separately bars liveries from renting a PWC to anyone under 16.
source_note: NY Navigation Law Section 73-a(2)(a), livery rental age minimum

question: Before renting out a personal watercraft, what must a New York livery operator do for the renter?
choice_a: Nothing beyond collecting payment for the rental
choice_b: Provide instruction and a demonstration of safe operating procedures and required safety equipment, by video or on the water, and confirm the renter can operate competently
choice_c: Check only that the renter has a driver's license, with no operating instruction required
choice_d: Hand over a printed brochure, with any demonstration left entirely optional
explanation: New York Navigation Law Section 73-a requires liveries to instruct and demonstrate safe operating procedures and safety equipment use to renters, by video or in-water demonstration, and to confirm the renter can operate the PWC and its safety equipment competently before rental.
source_note: NY Navigation Law Section 73-a(2)(b)-(c), livery instruction and competency requirement

question: What must a New York PWC livery keep on record for each rental, and for how long?
choice_a: Nothing; New York law does not require liveries to keep any rental records
choice_b: Only the renter's credit card number, retained indefinitely
choice_c: The renter's name, address, and age, along with vessel details, retained for at least one year
choice_d: A log of fuel purchased, retained for 30 days
explanation: New York Navigation Law Section 73-a requires liveries to record each renter's name, address, and age, along with vessel information, and to retain those records for at least one year.
source_note: NY Navigation Law Section 73-a(2)(e), livery recordkeeping requirement

question: Under New York Navigation Law Section 73-a, what is the fine range for a first-time violation of the PWC operating requirements?
choice_b: There is no monetary fine, only a written warning
explanation: A first violation of Section 73-a's PWC requirements carries a fine of $50 to $200, with higher fines for repeat violations within 24 months and eventual registration revocation for a third or subsequent violation.
source_note: NY Navigation Law Section 73-a(3)(a), penalty schedule

question: Does New York's PWC operating law (Navigation Law Section 73-a) apply to a professional performer during an authorized exhibition, or to a participant in an authorized race, regatta, or marine event?
choice_a: No, such performers and authorized race, regatta, or marine event participants are exempt from these operating restrictions during the sanctioned activity
choice_b: Yes, with no exemption available for any organized event
choice_c: Only professional performers are exempt; authorized race participants are not
choice_d: Exemptions under this section apply only to law enforcement PWCs
explanation: Section 73-a exempts professional exhibition performers and participants in an authorized race, regatta, or marine event from its standard PWC operating restrictions during the sanctioned activity.
source_note: NY Navigation Law Section 73-a(1)(h), professional/regatta exemption
